explicacion.en: The written accent goes on the ending in every future form except nosotros: hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablarán, but hablaremos.

titulo.en: The simple future: one word for “will”

texto.en: English says “I will talk” with two words. Spanish uses one: hablaré. To form the future, keep the whole infinitive (hablar, comer, vivir) and add the endings -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án. The endings are the same for -ar, -er and -ir verbs. Every form has a written accent except nosotros: hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablarán. The stress falls on the ending: ha-bla-RÉ, ha-bla-RÁS. You already know ir a + infinitive for near plans; the future is very common for appointments, promises and polite plans: Te llamaré a las cuatro. Nos veremos el martes. Useful time markers: mañana, el lunes, la próxima semana, el año que viene.
Same endings for every verb. Tap each form to hear it.

titulo.en: I will have, I will make, I will come

objetivo.en: Say who will come, what they will do and what they will be able to do at a party with the irregular future.

explicacion.en: Tener has an irregular future stem: tendr-. Do not add the endings to the full infinitive: tendré, tendrás, tendrá.
Hacer has the short stem har-: haré, harás, hará, haremos, harán.
Venir changes to the stem vendr-: vendré, vendrás, vendrá, vendremos, vendrán.

texto.en: Some common verbs do not use the full infinitive to make the future. They change the stem, but the endings stay exactly the same as before: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án. The stems to learn: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-, salir → saldr-, venir → vendr-, poner → pondr-, decir → dir-. Notice the pattern: in several of them the vowel before the r drops out and a d takes its place (tendr-, saldr-, vendr-, pondr-), and hacer and decir become shorter (har-, dir-). So you say tendré, never teneré. Use them for plans and promises: Vendré a tu fiesta. Haré el pastel. Saldré a las seis. Podré venir means “I will be able to come.”
Same endings as the regular future. Tap each form to hear it.

titulo.en: It's sunny today, it will rain tomorrow

objetivo.en: Talk about the weather in Quito and make simple predictions for today and tomorrow.

nota.en: El clima de Quito = the weather in Quito.

explicacion.en: English says “it is cold”, but Spanish uses hacer for sun, cold, heat and wind: hace frío, hace calor, hace sol, hace viento.
Frío, calor, sol and viento are nouns here, so use mucho, not muy: hace mucho frío, hace mucho calor.
Llover changes o → ue only in the present (llueve). In the future it keeps the o: lloverá.

texto.en: To talk about the weather, Spanish uses three patterns. First, hace + noun: hace sol, hace frío, hace calor, hace viento. Use mucho to say “very”: hace mucho frío (not “muy frío”). Second, está + adjective for the sky: está nublado, está despejado (clear). Third, a single verb for rain: llueve (llover changes o → ue). For tomorrow, use the future: hará frío, estará nublado, lloverá. In Quito people joke about “four seasons in one day”: cold in the morning, sun at noon and rain in the afternoon. October is part of the rainy season.
Today and tomorrow. Tap each phrase to hear it.

titulo.en: I'm planning to go… What if we go to the museum?

objetivo.en: Say what you plan to do and suggest or change a plan with ¿Y si…?, ¿Qué tal si…? and mejor.

traduccion.en: to plan / to intend (with an infinitive)

nota.en: Pienso ir = I plan to go. Pensar changes e → ie: pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, piensan.

nota.en: In Quito it goes up the Pichincha volcano and has a great view.

traduccion.en: the walk / the outing

nota.en: Reflexive: me quedo, nos quedamos. Nos quedamos en casa = We stay home.

traduccion.en: better / we'd better

nota.en: Mejor + present changes a plan: Mejor vamos mañana.

explicacion.en: After pensar, the infinitive follows directly: no a and no de. Pienso ir = I'm planning to go.
Pensar changes e → ie in yo, tú, él and ellos: pienso, piensas, piensa, piensan. Only nosotros keeps the e: pensamos.
After ¿Y si…? and ¿Qué tal si…? Spanish uses the present, not the future: ¿Y si vamos…?

titulo.en: Plans, suggestions and changes of plan

texto.en: Three tools for talking about plans. 1) Pensar + infinitive says what you intend to do: pienso ir al Panecillo (I plan to go to the Panecillo). Pensar changes e → ie, except for nosotros: pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, piensan. Do not add a or de before the infinitive. 2) To suggest something, use ¿Y si + present…? or ¿Qué tal si + present…?: ¿Y si vamos al museo? (What if we go to the museum?), ¿Qué tal si comemos afuera? (How about eating outside?). Both take the present tense, never the future. 3) To change a plan, use mejor + present: Mejor vamos mañana (We'd better go tomorrow), Mejor nos quedamos en casa (We'd better stay home).
Pensar changes e → ie, except nosotros. Tap each form to hear it.

explicacion.en: The pattern needs de: acabar de + infinitive. Without de, the meaning is lost.
After acabar de use the infinitive, not the gerund (-ando or -iendo). Acabamos de comer = We just ate.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Mejor nos vemos a las once.

explicacion.en: To change a plan with mejor, use the present: Mejor nos vemos a las once.

texto.en: To say that something happened a moment ago, Spanish uses acabar de + infinitive: Acabo de llegar means “I just arrived”. Conjugate only acabar (acabo, acabas, acaba, acabamos, acaban), then add de and the infinitive. Use acabar in the present, even though the action is already done: Acabo de salir = I just left. Do not use the gerund after it (not acabo llegando). You can add hace un momento (a moment ago) for emphasis. This pattern is very useful when you change a plan by phone: Acabo de ver mi agenda y mejor nos vemos mañana. Think of the whole pattern as a short way to say “just”.
Only acabar changes. Tap each form to hear it.
